newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors ask court to drop tycoons' appeal.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors ask court to drop tycoons' appeal.

text.p: State prosecutors on Thursday asked a South Korean court to reject appeals by two business tycoons sentenced to jail terms for bribing former president Roh Tae-woo, court officials said.

The appeals were made by Kim Woo-choong, the founder and chairman of Daewoo Group, against his two-year jail sentence, and Choi Won-suk, chairman of Dong-Ah Construction Industrial who was given a 2-1/2 year term.
"The prosecution demanded appeals by the defendants be rejected so that their sentences will be confirmed," an official at the Seoul High Court said.

Roh was sentenced to a 22-1/2 year jail term after being convicted of taking 283.8 billion won ($343 million) in bribes, and playing major roles in a 1979 military coup and the army massacre of pro-democracy protesters the following year.
Roh, who is also appealing his sentence, is being tried separately.
